page: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is a graphics-intensive virtual machine powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz. For hardware acceleration, the instance includes a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 22 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of 1880 GB of NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The system excels in specialized tasks, achieving top 25% results in Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient, though large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also strong, processing 62.3 million operations per second.

Large Language Model inference benchmarks reveal a distinct performance profile. For small and medium models, both prompt processing and text generation speeds reach the top 10% tier. However, scaling to a large 70B model highlights hardware limitations: while prompt processing remains strong, text generation throughput drops to the bottom 25% tier due to the single GPU configuration and VRAM constraints.

This hardware profile offers a balanced resource density for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. It is highly suited for medium-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and database-backed applications. The inclusion of local NVMe storage and dedicated CPU cores provides predictable performance, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require GPU acceleration without the overhead of multi-GPU clusters.
